chapter_title: The Interpretation [of] the S[i]lence, the Fast, [the Peace], the Day, [and] the Rest; [what] they are.
chapter_note: Despite the chapter title’s ritual-sounding keywords (silence/fast/peace/day/rest), the surviving content is mostly cosmological identification/exposition (First Man, ship of living waters, Pillar of Glory, great aeon). The only clear editorial layer is the opening dialogue-question frame and a closing beatitude/doxology. Several paragraphs are heavily lacunose; where a teaching paragraph includes an explicit teacher-attribution (“the enlightener ...”), that phrase is treated as later framing and stripped, leaving the underlying cosmological explanation.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue/Q&A frame: disciples question the enlightener; petition formula (“We implore you, our father...”). This is compiling-community apparatus, not the systematic substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the gatherer in [... ...] [...] is the Pill[a]r of Gl[or]y [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed surrounding ascetic-ethical/moralizing clauses about the body and “lusts of the world” and “righteousness,” which shift from cosmic identification to practical/moral application. Also excluded the manuscript page marker ⟨p.47⟩.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the cosmological identification of a ‘gatherer’ with the Pillar of Glory (a fixed element of Manichaean cosmic mechanics). The adjacent language about bodily lusts reads as interpretive/ascetic application rather than impersonal system-description.

paragraphs.core_text: The one they call [...] it is the [Fi]rst [M]an who dwel[ls i]n the ship of living waters [...] li]ght [...] he is c[alled ...] that they have [...] glorious [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal mapping/identification: a named cosmic hypostasis (First Man) located in a defined cosmic vehicle/domain (ship of living waters). No address to church practice, no citation, no institutional polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] cal]l it 'day' [...] uni]verse as they shall [...] in the great aeon [...] are spread in the universe, it is [...] established in the [...] and the so[u]ls [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explicit teacher-attribution phrase “[...] the enlighten[er ...” as dialogue/frame material (Layer 2 attribution) while retaining the cosmological explanation that follows.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is impersonal cosmological exposition (great aeon; distribution/establishment in the universe; relation to souls). The intrusion of “the enlightener ...” signals a later dialogic presentation layer wrapped around older teaching.
Beatitude/doxological close (“Blessed is he... remains for ever and ever”), characteristic of devotional/pastoral stitching rather than systematic cosmological correspondence-teaching.
